Find the number of all possible game processes.

Analysis: Recall the distance formula between two points. The expression \((\sqrt{2}\cos x - y)^2+\left(\sqrt{2}\sin x-\frac{9}{y}\right)^2\) can be regarded as the square of the distance between point \(A(\sqrt{2}\cos x,\sqrt{2}\sin x)\) and point \(B\left(y,\frac{9}{y}\right)\) in the plane rectangular coordinate system. informal_statement:
Let \(a, b, c, d\) be real numbers not all equal to \(0\). Find the maximum value of
\[
f=\frac{ab + 2bc+cd}{a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}+d^{2}}
\]

Proof: If we assume that the maximum value of \(f\) is \(M\), then
\[
ab + 2bc+cd\leqslant M(a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}+d^{2})
\]
Therefore, we need to establish an inequality of the above form and find a set of values of \(a, b, c, d\) for which the equality of the inequality holds.

Let \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma>0\). Then
\[
\frac{\alpha}{2}a^{2}+\frac{b^{2}}{2\alpha}\geqslant ab,\quad\beta b^{2}+\frac{c^{2}}{\beta}\geqslant 2bc,\quad\frac{\gamma}{2}c^{2}+\frac{d^{2}}{2\gamma}\geqslant cd
\]

Adding the above three inequalities, we get
\[
\begin{gathered}
\frac{\alpha}{2}a^{2}+\left(\frac{1}{2\alpha}+\beta\right)b^{2}+\left(\frac{1}{\beta}+\frac{\gamma}{2}\right)c^{2}+\frac{d^{2}}{2\gamma}\\
\geqslant ab + 2bc+cd
\end{gathered}
\]

Let \(\frac{\alpha}{2}=\frac{1}{2\alpha}+\beta=\frac{1}{\beta}+\frac{\gamma}{2}=\frac{1}{2\gamma}\). We get \(\gamma=\frac{1}{\alpha}\), \(\beta=\frac{1}{2}\left(\alpha-\frac{1}{\alpha}\right)\), and \(\alpha^{4}-6\alpha^{2} + 1=0\). Solving the equation, we obtain \(\alpha=\sqrt{2}+1\) (the other three solutions do not meet the requirements). Then
\[
\begin{gathered}
\frac{\sqrt{2}+1}{2}(a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}+d^{2})\geqslant ab + 2bc+cd\\
f\leqslant\frac{\sqrt{2}+1}{2}
\end{gathered}
\]

Moreover, when \(a = d = 1\), \(b=c=\sqrt{2}+1\), the equality of the inequality holds. So the maximum value of \(f\) is \(\frac{\sqrt{2}+1}{2}\).

theorem quantitative_reasoning_zh_blue_866 {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (a : Fin n → ℝ)
    (ha : ∀ i, 0 < a i) (p q : ℝ) (hp : 0 < p) (hq : 0 < q)
    (S : ℝ) (hS : S = (∑ i, (a i)^p) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / p)) :
    ∀ i : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), ∑ k, (a k^q - a (i k)^q) / (S^p - a k^p) ≥ 0 := by
informal_statement:
(Generalized form of W. Janous inequality)
Let \(a_1, a_2, \cdots, a_n \in \mathbf{R}^{+}\), \(p, q \in \mathbf{R}^{+}\). Denote \(S = (a_1^p + a_2^p+\cdots+a_n^p)^{\frac{1}{p}}\). Then for any permutation \(i_1, i_2, \cdots, i_n\) of \(1, 2, \cdots, n\), we have: \(\sum_{k = 1}^n\frac{a_k^q - a_{i_k}^q}{S^p - a_k^p}\geqslant0\).

Proof: By symmetry, without loss of generality, assume \(a_1\geqslant a_2\geqslant\cdots\geqslant a_n\). Then
\[
\sum_{j = 1}^k a_j^q\geqslant\sum_{j = 1}^k a_{i_j}^q(1\leqslant k\leqslant n - 1),\sum_{j = 1}^n a_j^q=\sum_{j = 1}^n a_{i_j}^q,
\]
and \((S^p - a_k^p)^{-1}\geqslant(S^p - a_{k + 1}^p)^{-1}(1\leqslant k\leqslant n - 1)\).
By the partial summation formula, we have \(\sum_{k = 1}^n\frac{a_k^q - a_{i_k}^q}{S^p - a_k^p}=(S^p - a_n^p)^{-1}\cdot\sum_{j = 1}^n(a_j^q - a_{i_j}^q)+\sum_{k = 1}^{n - 1}\left[\sum_{j = 1}^k(a_j^q - a_{i_j}^q)\right]\cdot\left[(S^p - a_k^p)^{-1}-(S^p - a_{k + 1}^p)^{-1}\right]\geqslant0\). Thus the original inequality holds.
